Implementation: - Rule implemented at src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts - Detects legacy @story + @req in block/JSDoc comments via analyzeComment/processComment. - Ignores comments that have only @story, only @req, or only @supports. - Reports: - messageId "preferImplements" for simple single-story legacy blocks. - messageId "cannotAutoFix" when mixed @story/@req and @supports are present, with reason "comment mixes @story/@req with existing @supports annotations". - messageId "multiStoryDetected" when multiple distinct @story paths are present. - Auto-fix implementation: - collectStoryAndReqMetadata extracts exactly one @story path and all simple @req IDs (form: "@story ", "@req "). - buildImplementsAutoFix returns a fixer only when: - storyPaths.size === 1 - storyLineIndices.length === 1 - reqLineIndices.length >= 1 - storyPath !== null - applyImplementsReplacement constructs a replacement line: - "@supports ${storyPath} ${reqIds.join(' ')}" - Preserves original line prefix/indentation and JSDoc "*" markers. - Replaces the @story line, removes @req lines, leaves all other lines untouched (preserving order of description/params and other tags). - Rule meta.fixable is set to "code", enabling ESLint --fix. - Multi-story detection uses MULTI_STORY_THRESHOLD = 1 and hasMultipleStories(storyPaths) to gate auto-fix; complex patterns receive diagnostics only (no fix), satisfying conservative behavior. - JSDoc at top of file references docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md and enumerates REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT, REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION, REQ-AUTO-FIX.

traceability.notes: The story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS is fully implemented. The prefer-implements-annotation rule exists and is wired into the plugin, is disabled by default, and can be configured to off/warn/error via standard ESLint severity. It detects legacy @story + @req usage, issues recommendation warnings, and provides a conservative auto-fix that converts simple single-story, single-path blocks (with one or many simple @req lines) into a single @supports line while preserving comment structure and tag ordering. Multi-story and mixed @story/@req/@supports patterns are detected and reported without auto-fix. Legacy @story/@req annotations continue to validate correctly when the rule is disabled, and the auto-fix output is compatible with existing @supports validation rules. Comprehensive tests (including configuration and auto-fix behavior) plus dedicated documentation (rule docs and migration guide) confirm that all acceptance criteria and enumerated requirements for this story are met.
